newsitem.title: MEXICO: CoreStates buys stake in Mexican exchange house.
newsitem.headline: CoreStates buys stake in Mexican exchange house.

text.p: The U.S. bank CoreStates has bought a 20 percent stake in the Mexican currency exchange house Vectodivisas, a subsidiary of the Vector brokerage, Vector said on Wednesday.
CoreStates made the acquisition using its subsidiary Philadelphia International Equities Inc (PIE), Vector said in a statement.

"The investment by CoreStates is compatible with our strategy of looking for world-class partners and attracting foreign investment," Adrian Rodriguez, chairman of Vectodivisas, said in the statement.
PIE Director James Pope said in the statement that the deal would "extend our international network and provide services in Mexico."
PIE, founded in 1981, operates in Asia, Europe, the United States, Latin American and Britain, the statement said.
Vectodivisas, founded in 1989, is one of the five most active exchange houses in Mexico, the statement said.
